prompt: Write a complete Python module that implements an LRU cache with TTL, thread safety, statistics (hits, misses, evictions), a decorator interface, and a small self-test under __main__. Include docstrings and type hints.

Write a complete, production-ready Python module using asyncio that implements a token-bucket rate limiter, a sliding-window concurrency limiter, per-key rate limiting with periodic cleanup, an async retry decorator with exponential backoff and full jitter, structured metrics tracking (allowed, throttled, retries, total wait time), and a thorough self-test suite under __main__. Include full type hints, docstrings, and complete implementations of every method without placeholders.

Write a complete Python module that implements a durable log-structured key-value store backed by an append-only write-ahead log (WAL) with CRC32 record checksums, tombstone deletes, an in-memory keydir index rebuilt on startup, atomic segment rotation and compaction, prefix range scans, snapshot export to SQLite, and a comprehensive self-test under __main__. Include full docstrings, type hints, and complete code with no omitted sections.

Write a complete Python module that implements a tokenizer, recursive-descent parser, typed AST node hierarchy, and evaluator for an expression language supporting integers, floats, booleans, variables, arithmetic (+, -, *, /, //, %, **), comparisons (==, !=, <, <=, >, >=), logical operators (and, or, not), ternary conditionals, built-in math functions, and detailed syntax error messages with line and column positions. Include an AST pretty-printer, a constant-folding optimizer pass, full docstrings, type hints, and a thorough unit test suite under __main__.

Write a complete, single-file CUDA C++ program that implements a baseline naive matrix transpose kernel, a tiled shared-memory transpose kernel with +1 column padding to eliminate shared-memory bank conflicts, and a vectorized float4 variant for aligned dimensions. Include CUDA error checking macros, non-multiple-of-tile-size bounds handling, CUDA event timing with effective GB/s bandwidth calculation, CPU reference verification across multiple matrix shapes, and a complete main() CLI benchmark harness with detailed comments.

Write a complete Python module that implements a multi-threaded work-stealing task scheduler with per-worker double-ended queues, directed acyclic graph (DAG) task dependencies, cycle detection before execution, task cancellation and timeout handling, exception propagation to dependent tasks, execution timeline statistics, and an extensive unittest suite under __main__. Include complete docstrings, type hints, and full method bodies without any stubs.
Write a 900-word essay on how a homelab operator should think about power, heat and noise when running eight passive datacenter GPUs in a home office, with concrete numbers and trade-offs.

Write a detailed 1,000-word technical analysis of NVMe storage tiering, ZFS ARC and L2ARC sizing, special allocation vdevs, and SSD write amplification in home and small-lab servers. Cover concrete RAM-to-L2ARC metadata ratios, recordsize tuning for mixed virtual machine and model checkpoint workloads, endurance math in DWPD and TBW, and failure-domain trade-offs. Use full paragraphs with quantitative examples.

Write a thorough 1,000-word engineering postmortem narrative describing a silent multi-node distributed cache corruption incident caused by an overlooked serialization schema drift and partial key-hash mismatch during a rolling upgrade. Cover the timeline from initial anomaly detection through root-cause isolation, blast-radius quantification, data repair procedures, and concrete architectural safeguards added afterward.

Write a comprehensive 1,000-word technical essay comparing static ahead-of-time deterministic compiler optimizations against profile-guided optimization (PGO) and dynamic JIT runtime specialization in modern systems. Analyze code layout, branch prediction, devirtualization, inlining heuristics, tail-latency warm-up penalties, reproducibility constraints, and operational complexity with concrete examples.

Write a detailed 1,000-word architectural essay on designing reliable offline-first local AI appliances under strict residential power and thermal budgets. Discuss memory bandwidth versus compute bottlenecks, quantization trade-offs, silent hardware fault detection, UPS graceful shutdown orchestration, acoustic engineering, and unattended service recovery with concrete design numbers.

Write a detailed 1,000-word historical and technical essay on PCIe link generations (Gen3 through Gen6), Base Address Register (BAR) apertures and Above-4G decoding, posted writes versus non-posted reads, completion credits, root-complex versus switch-fabric peer-to-peer DMA bottlenecks, and how IOMMU and ACS settings affect multi-GPU collective transfers.
Produce a JSON array of 40 objects describing fictional PCIe devices. Each object has keys vendor, device, bus_id, link_gen, link_width, bar1_mib, notes (one sentence). Output JSON only.

Produce a JSON array of 30 objects representing datacenter rack power distribution unit (PDU) sensors. Each object must have keys sensor_id, rack, bus, phase, voltage_v, amperage_a, temp_c, status, and notes (one detailed sentence). Output valid JSON only with all 30 entries and no surrounding markdown or commentary.

Produce a complete JSON object containing an OpenAPI 3.1 style specification for a 10-endpoint distributed job queue REST API (submit job, get job, list jobs, cancel job, retry job, heartbeat, fetch logs, list workers, drain worker, and queue metrics). Include paths, HTTP methods, parameter definitions, full request and response JSON schemas, and structured error code schemas for 400, 401, 404, 409, 429, and 503 responses. Output valid JSON only with no markdown fences or extra text.

Produce a JSON array of 30 objects representing synthetic Linux kernel ftrace and perf trace events during a high-throughput NVMe and network I/O burst. Each object must have keys timestamp_us, cpu, pid, comm, event_type, duration_us, subsystem, and payload (an object with 3 to 4 concrete numeric or string fields). Output valid JSON only with all 30 entries and no commentary.

Produce a JSON array of 25 objects describing compiler optimization passes across mid-end IR and backend code generation. Each object must have keys pass_id, stage, ir_level, complexity, preserves_cfg, dependencies (array of pass_id strings), and description (one detailed technical sentence). Output valid JSON only with all 25 entries and no surrounding text.

Produce a JSON array of 30 objects representing synthetic ZFS storage pool scrub and SMART drive health snapshots across multiple vdevs. Each object must have keys pool, vdev, device, media, temp_c, wear_pct, read_err, write_err, cksum_err, and action (one concrete operator recommendation sentence). Output valid JSON only with all 30 entries and no commentary.
